bug_semantics: A scoped access token carrying only profile:read is accepted by PUT /user because that state-changing route is guarded with RequireScopes(ScopeProfileRead). UpdateUser derives the target from the token viewer, checks only that the target user is an administrator, and permits a supplied password to replace the administrator password. The attacker can then log in with that password; login issues a session-typed JWT, and RequireScopes deliberately bypasses all scope checks for session tokens, yielding an unrestricted administrator session.
flaw_origin: PR #195 introduced the scoped-token authorization feature. Its atomic member b47fa1c75d890cd080e3f6699bbfca8cd8d4b939 first wrote the security-significant mismatch in internal/router/user.go by binding the write-capable PUT /user handler to ScopeProfileRead. GitHub later squashed the PR into main as 3f8fb150158723aca31df2ae937a1aa7b31ac254; that aggregate is a carrier, not the smallest BIC.
ai_marker: BIC commit-object metadata identifies human author and committer L1nSn0w/lin-snow (not a bot) and contains the exact trailer "Made-with: Cursor"; it contains no Co-Authored-By or Generated-with trailer. The explicit Cursor trailer is commit-object AI-assistance evidence, but attribution is shared/weaker than an AI author or co-author.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/lin-snow/Ech0/security/advisories/GHSA-hm2h-wwwh-g49x describes the exact chain: profile:read access token -> PUT /user password change -> POST /login -> unrestricted session token. It names internal/router/user.go, internal/service/user/user.go, internal/middleware/scope.go, and internal/util/jwt/jwt.go, and lists patched version 4.4.3. Its package table says affected <=4.2.1, while the repository history and the global advisory summary establish that the vulnerable route persists after 4.2.1 through 4.4.2; this audit uses the directly verified Git boundary rather than silently inheriting that table inconsistency.

In the validated clone, `git log -L 39,44:internal/router/user.go v4.4.2 --format=fuller` and `git log -p -S'middleware.RequireScopes(authModel.ScopeProfileRead)' -- internal/router/user.go` both attribute the vulnerable mainline line to one-parent squash carrier 3f8fb150158723aca31df2ae937a1aa7b31ac254 and show 057e8b0b713d105eca7040ade810a057397613fa replacing ProfileRead with ProfileWrite.

PR decomposition is reproducible from https://github.com/lin-snow/Ech0/pull/195/commits and https://github.com/lin-snow/Ech0/commit/b47fa1c75d890cd080e3f6699bbfca8cd8d4b939.patch. The patch header gives the full member SHA and its internal/router/user.go diff adds `middleware.RequireScopes(authModel.ScopeProfileRead)` directly between the PUT /user route and UpdateUser handler. The public commit object's embedded metadata gives parent 1b280c252d1ef2ee69bf09f890d2da673b4b0a68, author and committer lin-snow, and body trailer `Made-with: Cursor`.

Direct parent-tree verification: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lin-snow/Ech0/1b280c252d1ef2ee69bf09f890d2da673b4b0a68/internal/router/user.go contains the pre-BIC single-line `AuthRouterGroup.PUT("/user", h.UserHandler.UpdateUser())`, has no authModel import, and has no RequireScopes/ProfileRead guard. Thus the specific read-scope-on-write flawed line is absent from the immediate BIC parent.

At vulnerable tag v4.4.2, `git blame -L 270,305 v4.4.2 -- internal/service/user/user.go` shows UpdateUser taking viewer.UserID, requiring only user.IsAdmin, and assigning `user.Password = cryptoUtil.MD5Encrypt(userdto.Password)` at lines 274-302. `git blame -L 14,24 v4.4.2 -- internal/middleware/scope.go` shows session tokens immediately call ctx.Next at lines 17-19. `git blame -L 28,42 v4.4.2 -- internal/util/jwt/jwt.go` shows login claims are Type TokenTypeSession at line 33. Together these source facts reproduce the advisory's escalation path.

Direct closure: `git diff 2ccf950dcbb582b1c24147d0783a3397e9fe7354 057e8b0b713d105eca7040ade810a057397613fa -- internal/model/auth/scope.go internal/router/user.go internal/middleware/scope_test.go` adds ScopeProfileWrite to the valid scope set, changes PUT /user and the other profile-mutating routes from ProfileRead to ProfileWrite, and adds regression cases proving ProfileRead receives 403 while ProfileWrite succeeds. The fix parent is 2ccf950dcbb582b1c24147d0783a3397e9fe7354, so 057e8b0b713d105eca7040ade810a057397613fa is the direct mechanism reversal despite its unrelated inbox-removal subject.

Release boundary in the clone: `git tag --contains 3f8fb150158723aca31df2ae937a1aa7b31ac254` starts at v4.2.1, while `git merge-base --is-ancestor 3f8fb150158723aca31df2ae937a1aa7b31ac254 v4.2.0` exits 1. The same contains query shows the carrier in v4.4.2. `git merge-base --is-ancestor 057e8b0b713d105eca7040ade810a057397613fa v4.4.2` exits 1, while `git tag --contains 057e8b0b713d105eca7040ade810a057397613fa` starts at v4.4.3. Therefore v4.2.1 is the first affected tag, v4.4.2 remains vulnerable, and v4.4.3 is the first fixed tag.

BIC-only AI check: the embedded commit object at https://github.com/lin-snow/Ech0/commit/b47fa1c75d890cd080e3f6699bbfca8cd8d4b939 records authors=[lin-snow], committer=lin-snow, parents=[1b280c252d1ef2ee69bf09f890d2da673b4b0a68], and body `Add RequireScopes ...\n\nMade-with: Cursor`. No later commit, PR-body statement, branch name, squash-carrier-only attribution, or fix attribution is used for the verdict.
reasoning: The vulnerability is an authorization-contract error, not a password-handler origin: UpdateUser's administrator password mutation predates scoped tokens, but PR #195 newly promised least-privilege route scopes and then classified the write route as profile:read. Mainline -L/-S history identifies the PR squash, and the recoverable PR member history narrows that carrier to b47fa1c75d890cd080e3f6699bbfca8cd8d4b939, the member that first wrote the exact flawed guard. Its direct parent tree lacks that guard, so this is not a move, refactor, release commit, or fix. The omnibus fix 057e8b0b713d105eca7040ade810a057397613fa directly reverses the mismatch by introducing profile:write and changing the route, with v4.4.3 as the first containing release. The BIC itself explicitly says `Made-with: Cursor`, while both author and committer are the human maintainer; this proves AI-assisted causally flawed code but only shared/weaker attribution, so AI_CODE_FLAWED is more precise than AI_ROOT_CAUSE.
